Notes: Each row cites the exact native sequence and request ID; source timestamps use existing At convention. Native caller user and trust principal rebind to replay caller root; owned prefix/account rebind deterministically.

Duplicate TagResource requests include a distinct sentinel tag, and duplicate access-point UntagResource requests include a distinct existing keep key. Subsequent native tag sets prove rejection is all-or-nothing for the captured inputs.
Tag arrays retain native ordering but are sets, not an AWS ordering guarantee.

Bucket duplicate creation/removal 500s and unchanged/absent post-state are replayed as repeatably captured rejection contracts on fresh low-cardinality resources, corroborated by prior captures and a quiet-interval removal retry. This does not assert a universal permanent AWS validation code or generalize AP InvalidTag to buckets.

Only reached authority endpoint states are replayed after the captured mutations. All measured delays and stale decisions remain raw; endpoint selection is not a latency SLA or a local delay requirement.
Transient quota errors are archive-only. The successful replacement and its observed tag set establish recovered capacity without pinning how long recovery takes.
Randomized IAM role identifiers, session credentials and access-point alias outputs are intentionally unasserted, matching existing native replay conventions.
